title: Claude Max ($100) vs ChatGPT Pro / Codex ($100) for solo mobile game dev?
author: EvrenSasmaz
selftext:
​

Hey everyone,

I'm a solo dev working on a 3D mobile game and looking to put around $100–$120/month into one main AI coding subscription. Right now I'm torn between Claude Max ($100) and ChatGPT Pro ($100 for Codex), especially with OpenAI just dropping GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol.

For context, I already have an active Tripo AI subscription for 3D asset generation. Ideally, I want to automate as much of my asset-to-engine workflow as possible  alongside core gameplay coding, shaders, UI, and mobile optimization.

If anyone here is using either of these $100 plans for game dev, I'd love to know:

1. Real-world limits on long sessions: ChatGPT Pro removes the 5-hour rolling limit and only has a weekly cap, while Claude Max gives 5x Pro usage but still keeps that 5-hour window. If you're doing 4-6 hour dev sprints, do you actually hit the wall on Claude Max?

2. Code quality on game architecture;  How do the new GPT-6.2 models in Codex handle larger game codebases (state machines, refactoring, physics/UI bugs) compared to Claude Code with Opus 5.5? 

3. 3D / Engine pipeline: Has anyone hooked up Tripo 3D (via CLI, MCP, or Codex plugins) into their Unity/Godot workflow with either of these?

Appreciate any real-world feedback before I lock in a sub for the month!

comments.author: WhosLive
comments.body: Usually the subscription matters less than how you structure the sessions. Long game dev sprints tend to go better when you keep a short design doc and a task list in the repo, so a fresh session can pick up without re-reading everything. A lot of people split the work, with one model for architecture and refactors and the other for quick shader or UI fixes. For the Tripo pipeline, it's worth testing a single asset end to end (generate, export glTF, import, set up materials) before committing, since that's where most of the glue code ends up. Since both plans are month to month, running one for a few weeks on your real project is probably the best test.

replies.author: EvrenSasmaz
replies.body: this is close to what i already do actually. i have a gdd in the repo that the model keeps updated as we work, plus it also updates my obsidian vault. so my question is more specific: even witha short doc, every fresh session the model still reads all of that back, and even typing "where was i" at the start eats 10-15% of my plan. does the doc approach actually make that cheaper, oris it the same cost either way? and am i over-clearing? maybe the real answer is just to clear less and let the session run longer.

replies.author: WhosLive
replies.body:
Short answer: the doc helps, but only if the model reads a small part of it. Cost scales with how much text gets loaded into the session, so a GDD plus an Obsidian vault read back every time costs about the same as no doc at all.

What usually works better:

- Keep a separate tiny "state" file (20-40 lines): current task, last thing finished, next step, open bugs. Start each session by pointing the model at just that file, not the whole GDD or vault.
- Avoid "where was I". That invites it to go explore the repo and read a bunch of files. Paste or reference the state note instead.
- Only pull in GDD sections when the task needs them ("read the combat section", not "read the GDD").

On clearing: yes, you might be over-clearing. Each clear means paying again to rebuild context. But very long sessions get pricey too, because every turn resends the whole history, and quality tends to drift. A decent middle ground is to clear at task boundaries, not mid-task, and have the model update the state file right before you clear.

comments.author: imlo2
comments.body:
Claude Code Lasts much longer if you use Opus 5.5, compared to if you use Codex and Astra on high thinking.  
I've so far been able to make Opus 5.5 last for full 7 days week of long work days (8-12 hours a day), while Astra on Codex run out in a long day or so. Again this week, in 2 days I already used full 7 days of usage, and not that many hours either.

I've never run out of 5 hour window with Opus 5.5 so far, but that's quite easily doable if you spawn multiple sub-agents, or use Fable. That eats the Max account usage quite fast. This is all without any special configurations.

I've not yet had time to use GPT-6.2 for anything, going to try it soon.

But in my opinion OpenAI's models are better for planning and supporting thinking/learning, if you do that in ChatGPT. So that's something to consider. Not that Claude is bad, but not everyone likes its style.

3D / Engine: it's now trivial to plug in almost "anything"; Blender MCP, Higgsfield, Scenario etc. are easy to put to use. I've used all of those. And same for local, if you host ComfyUI for locally running image generation or 3D models, you can then ask the model to set up the workflows or at least a template which you tune manually, but both Astra and Opus do so good work that I haven't needed to adjust anything manually anymore in ComfyUI graphs. Game engines are also relatively easy to use; Unity and Godot work well. I've set up Unity CLI and CoplayDev's MCP for most of my projects now.

replies.author: EvrenSasmaz
replies.body: ok this actually changes my situation a bit, i should have mentioned it. budget is tight so i'm thinking of buying just one month, and i only have free time for this for like 2-3 weeks anyway.right now i'm on two $20 opus plans and both of them burn out way too fast on opus 5.5 medium, my weekly limits are gone by day 3 or 4. so realistically i want to work 7-8 hours a day for a fewweeks without constantly hitting walls. based on what you said, max with opus 5.5 sounds like it would actually cover that? just want to make sure i'm not misreading your numbers, because thatwould be a huge upgrade from where i am now.

replies.author: imlo2
replies.body: I do have the $100 Max account (costs a bit more here, but it's that same tier). I've used today Opus 5.5 during 10 hours, and out of those I'd say it's been running 8 hours doing its thing, rest is what I've done in between - checking test results, looking at documents/code, etc. and my fresh week's usage (started last evening 10:00pm my local time) has been used up to 8% right now (it's 00:07 here, so already over a full day of time gone). All of this usage is so far *Opus 5.5 on Extra High thinking level*. You could save tokens if you reduce that quality level, and there's no point of wasting Opus on document reading, papers, organizing images, etc. etc. Also, you can configure all sub-agent reading and such work to be forced to use a lower tier model in the configuration file of either a project, or globally for Claude Code. When I started using Claude after using Codex, I almost felt like the usage meter was stuck, as it took so long time to consume one percent. But again I just want to repeat, be aware that Fable does use credits at much faster pace, so don't expect that $100 account to last full days with it. And on Max you can only use 50% of your week's budget with Fable.

replies.author: EvrenSasmaz
replies.body: Thanks for your comment. Do subagents read the entire session all over again?

replies.author: imlo2
replies.body: If you start a new fresh agent it starts with fresh context, but forked agents get existing context. So essentially they need to get their bearings first and read the documents, readme files etc. to understand what they are doing. But it's much cheaper if use Sonet etc. for that, and have the write summaries or other documentation, whatever works best for your way of working.

comments.author: NegativePoetry1561
comments.body:
OK, so I have now made the same game in Claude and ChatGPT and what I noticed is that ChatGPT is more token-expensive because it tests after every single freaking line of code it writes!

Claude codes the task and then tests it. So I prefer Claude tbh when it comes to coding in general, what is nice in Codex is that it can make the GFX too, something Claude can't do without a connection to an external AI.

In the end though I think that both are close to each other!

  
I recently made this port with Claude [https://horizon.forgottenpixel.com](https://horizon.forgottenpixel.com) now granted it was just the port that was made by Claude cause I already wrote the whole thing for over a year in SpriteKit for the Mac, but when I first tried it with ChatGPT it took 3 days and it still wasn't done. I was using a ChatGPT 200 account. Then I did it with a Claude Pro account and it did it in 1 day, had to take some breaks due to the 5 Hour limits, but worth it!
